_comment: Upstream changelog entries already triaged, keyed by release, scope and a digest of the entry. The sentences themselves are deliberately not stored: primeng.dev content is outside the MIT grant (CONTRIBUTING.md), so this file records OUR decisions, not their prose. Regenerate with: npm run watch:upstream -- --record

22.1.2 · Core · 209ab26cfbb6.note: REPRODUCED, then FIXED 2026-10-11 under Constitution P3.b (v1.4.0). This is audit finding W-2 (2026-08-28). bind.ts set every passthrough key as an attribute and also assigned it to the element property of the same name, with no sanitizer on either path. Measured on Chrome through a real agl-button (e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts): an image in pt's innerHTML ran its onerror, and a javascript: href on an aglBind link ran on click, while the same values through [innerHTML] and [href] stayed inert. An on* string did NOT run: the property assignment after setAttribute sets el.onclick to a string, which the browser turns into null, so the audit's second sink was wrong by reasoning alone. Fix: markup keys (innerHTML, outerHTML, srcdoc) and URL keys (href, src, action, formaction, xlink:href) go through Angular's sanitizer in the HTML and URL contexts, non-function on* values are not written, and DomSanitizer.bypassSecurityTrustHtml / bypassSecurityTrustUrl is the way back. Held with test.fail() until the fix.

22.1.0 · Highlights · 78a27a89212b.note: Same subject as Core 52ea729050b3, stated as a highlight rather than as a defect. Measured there 2026-09-05: REPRODUCES.

22.1.0 · Table · 9f85f9a516a5.note: REPRODUCED, then FIXED 2026-09-05 under Constitution P3.a (v1.3.0). The mechanism was not the one first suspected, and the register's own instruction — "Do not close this by reasoning" — is why that was caught: it is NOT clear(). onChanges() at table.ts:1200 copied the totalRecords input into _totalRecords only when simpleChange.totalRecords.firstChange was true, so every later change was dropped, and :1212 then wrote the stale copy back over the input Angular had just set. Because the binding expression had not changed on the next pass, Angular never corrected it. clear() at :2209 repeats the same expression and merely inherited the staleness. Measured in the browser 2026-09-04: shrinking five rows to two while declaring two left the paginator rendering three pages. Fix: mirror every change, not just the first. Held as test.fail() from 04-09 until the fix, which is what forced the conversion to an ordinary test. Guarded by e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts plus 4 specs in table.spec.ts; mutation-checked (restoring the firstChange guard turns 2 of them red).

22.1.0 · Core · 52ea729050b3.note: REPRODUCES here too — measured in the browser 2026-09-05 (e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts). Cross-cutting stays the right verdict, but the entry had sat with no note, so nobody had asked the question. usestyle.ts:25 resolves the insertion point as this.document.head and appends there; nothing in the tree calls getRootNode() and there is no option to nominate another container. Two identical agl-buttons, one in the light DOM and one inside ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom: background-color computes to rgb(16, 185, 129) and rgb(239, 239, 239) — the user-agent default for a button, meaning no library rule reached it. background-color was chosen because it is NOT an inherited property: design tokens are custom properties and DO cross a shadow boundary, so a token assertion would have reported success while the rule consuming the token never arrived. Called a LIMITATION rather than a defect — nothing here promises shadow-root support — but a consumer who puts angulux inside a web component gets an unstyled library and no diagnostic. Supporting it means giving useStyle a container to insert into, which is new API: Phase 2 under P3. Held as test.fail().

22.1.0 · Core · cdab24c28a4e.note: ALREADY FIXED here, before this register existed: 9007858 (2026-08-26) changed chipstyle.ts and toaststyle.ts from `x && 'value'` to a ternary, because && yields false and Angular 22 rejects false as a style value (NG0318, once per style per change detection). Recorded 2026-09-05 for completeness — the entry had been filed cross-cutting with no note, so nothing connected the sentence to the commit that answered it. Upstream names three components; the third, SpeedDial, is parked in attic/ and ships nowhere. Swept 2026-09-05: no other inlineStyles object in the shipped tree produces a boolean. The remaining && in style files are all class maps, where false is the correct value.

22.1.0 · Table · 3ae212c58d45.note: MEASURED IN THE BROWSER 2026-09-05 (e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts). The earlier verdict had the direction right and the mechanism wrong, and it was the only one of the five entries closed without running anything. WHAT WAS WRONG: it claimed "button.ts never reads buttonProps?.outlined, so outlined is ignored on EVERY agl-button". Measured false — a plain agl-button given only buttonProps={outlined:true} renders p-button-outlined. buttonstyle.ts:17 does read instance.buttonProps?.outlined, and the theme has exactly one selector for this, .p-button-outlined (angulux-styles/src/button/index.ts:314); the getter that omits buttonProps is dataP at button.ts:864, and the string data-p never appears in that stylesheet. WHAT IS REAL is narrower, and is exactly what upstream reported: the value cannot be turned OFF. table.ts:5394 hard-codes [outlined]="true" on the popover clear button and passes filterButtonProps?.popover?.clear beside it at :5398, and classes.root starts with instance.outlined || ..., so a false arriving through the props object has nothing left to decide. Measured on the real component: with popover.clear = { outlined: false, size: 'small' }, the button carrying data-pc-name="pcfilterclearbutton" renders p-button p-button-outlined p-button-sm — p-button-sm coming out of the SAME object, which proves the object arrived and was read and rules out "the input never got there". Held as test.fail(). Fix changes runtime behaviour: blocked by P3 in Phase 1.

22.1.0 · Table · 0c9d548f166c.note: DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Measured in the browser 2026-09-04 (e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts, ordinary passing test): with the body scrolled sideways, document.elementFromPoint over the frozen cell returns the frozen cell. The test asserts its own premise first — scrollLeft > 0, and a normal cell geometrically extending under the frozen column x-range — so a green result cannot come from nothing being underneath. The library contributes no z-index here; stacking comes from the theme CSS, which is why source could not answer it. Test kept as a regression guard.

22.1.0 · Table · d9c2f7aacdad.note: DOES NOT REPRODUCE. Measured in the browser 2026-09-04 (e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts, ordinary passing test): filter to one row, call clear(), and both things the mechanism predicted would break are fine — all three rows return AND the column filter input is empty. The in-place filter.value = null at table.ts:2213-2223 is real and hasFilter() does stay true, but neither consequence reaches the user here. Note also that the notEquals half of the earlier reasoning is moot: that defect was fixed under the first P3 exemption (filterservice.ts, 2026-08-26). Test kept as a regression guard.

22.1.0 · DatePicker · b3d68c790b2d.note: REPRODUCED, then FIXED 2026-09-05 under Constitution P3.a (v1.3.0). Measured in the browser 2026-09-04: with minDate and the value both at 09:00 on the same day, one step down rendered 11, not 09 — and updateTime() writes that through to the bound model, so the application declared a minimum of 09:00 and received a LATER time the user never chose, with nothing reported. The locus was two switch(true) branches in constrainTime whose bodies assigned a hard-coded 11 (one also set this.pm = true, on a path that only runs when the minimum is BEFORE noon). Inherited verbatim from 21.1.9. Fix: both branches removed. Each condition was a strict subset of a general minimum clamp further down the same switch, and those clamps assign the minimum itself; the minute and second lines they fell through into are repeated verbatim in those groups, so minute/second clamping is unchanged. Guarded by e2e/upstream-repro.spec.ts plus 5 specs in datepicker.spec.ts asserting the contract (never below the minimum, never past what was asked) rather than the absence of the literal 11; mutation-checked (assigning 11 in the general clamp turns 2 of them red).

22.1.0 · Select · fff76133ad6e.note: NOT OURS. angulux select has no `multiple` input — that property exists only in their v22. Nothing here can enter the state described.

22.1.0 · FilterService · 2d7b393e4c46.note: REPRODUCES, and FIXED. The note below said "blocked by P3" until 2026-09-05, and that had been untrue since 2026-08-26; correcting it is the only change. Proven at runtime against the BUILT package: FilterService.filter with an empty filter returned 0/3 rows for notEquals and 3/3 for equals/startsWith/contains/notContains (null, undefined and "" alike). filterservice.ts:101-103 returned false where every sibling returns true. isNot delegates to it and was fixed by the same line; dateIsNot carries its own guard and was NEVER affected — the first triage said otherwise and was wrong. Reachable from the UI: executeLocalFilter (table.ts:2142) has no blank guard, and columnFilter registers constraints with value: null. Fixed under the first P3 exemption in 9007858 (2026-08-26), which also added filterservice.spec.ts.

22.1.4 · DatePicker · 769fb13bdf0f.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, then FIXED 2026-11-03 under Constitution P3.a. In an inline picker with a minDate and weekends disabled, 19 day cells carry the p-disabled class and no element in the picker carries aria-disabled, neither the day span nor its td. The class is the only disabled signal, and a screen reader does not read classes. Fix: the day span carries aria-disabled="true" exactly when it carries p-disabled (before minDate, after maxDate, a disabled date or weekday, or the whole picker disabled). Condition 2 of P3.a: the inputs declare those days "disabled (not selectable)", and the picker withheld that from the accessibility tree. Held with test.fail() until the fix.

22.1.4 · Table · 5b2f43899b05.note: Does NOT reproduce, measured 2026-11-02. In a virtual-scroll table of 1,000 rows, a 200 px scroll keeps every row still in view as the same DOM element and adds only the rows that scrolled in; a resize recreates none. Kept as a passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts.

22.1.4 · DatePicker · 2c0b4d9bb30d.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, in the INLINE picker only. Enter on the next-month button moves the month and drops focus on <body>, because the header holding the button is rebuilt with the month and nothing puts focus back: the restore in the contentWrapper setter runs only when this.overlay is set, which an inline picker never sets. The popup keeps focus (ArrowLeft from 1 March lands on 28 February, PageDown on 28 March). Measured alongside: the inline day grid has no tabindex=0 cell, so Tab goes prev, month, year, next and then leaves the picker without reaching a day. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.4 · Table · 096a73ca9524.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, only when a column filter is declared. Without one, resetPageOnSort=false keeps page 3 on sort. With a <agl-columnFilter> in the header, page 3 becomes page 1: the filter registers an empty constraint when it starts, so hasFilter() is true from then on, and sortSingle() runs _filter(), which sets first = 0 and resets the scroll without reading resetPageOnSort. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.4 · Drawer · 717c3af903be.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, exactly as stated. In a ViewEncapsulation.ShadowDom host, opening a modal drawer throws "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'style')" from enableModality() and no mask is created. enableModality() counts open drawers with document.querySelectorAll('[data-p-open="true"]'), which does not see into a shadow root; with zero found it reads the entry at index -1. The same drawer in the light DOM opens with its mask and no error. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.3 · Table · 808f9fd0181d.note: Does NOT reproduce, measured 2026-11-02. The sort icon renders sort-alt on an unsorted column, sort-amount-down for an initial [sortOrder]="-1", and sort-amount-up-alt after a click, with aria-sort and p-datatable-column-sorted set. A static sortOrder="-1" attribute does not compile under strictTemplates (the input has no number transform), so it was not measured. Kept as a passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts.

22.1.3 · DatePicker · 05c817919d3e.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, as a date loss, then FIXED 2026-11-03 under Constitution P3.a. Typing 11:30 into a timeOnly picker bound to 2020-01-15 10:00 produced TODAY at 11:30: parseDateTime() builds a typed time on new Date() when timeOnly is set. The hour button on the same picker keeps the date (2020-01-15 11:00), so the two input paths disagree. Not reproduced: a 12-hour timeOnly picker with no value shows the current hour correctly (a reading of the source had predicted 00). Fix: a typed time is built on the date of the bound value, so it writes the instant the hour button writes; with no value it still starts from today. The date is remembered apart from the model, because typing empties the model on the way ("1" is not a time): a first version that read the model passed a unit test that set the whole string at once and failed the browser test, which types one key at a time. Held with test.fail() until the fix.

22.1.3 · MultiSelect · dca7c6429b5f.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, with [selectAll] bound to a field that was never assigned. onToggleAll() tests selectAll != null and allSelected() tests selectAll !== null, so undefined is uncontrolled to the first and an answer of undefined to the second: every click takes the select-all branch. The second click re-selects all four options and the checkbox shows unchecked over them. Unbound, and with a disabled option preselected, select-all and unselect-all both work. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.3 · Toast · ddf710dbc96a.note: Does NOT reproduce: angulux has no swipe-to-dismiss. toast.ts has no touch or pointer handler, so a swipe leaves every message in place and there is no half-dismissed state to leak. Measured 2026-11-02 with a real CDP touch swipe; the close button then removes the right message by index. Kept as a passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts.

22.1.3 · Table · ec1148b1cfc0.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, and the cause is CSS, not the component. Script time per render on Chrome: 1,000 / 2,000 / 4,000 / 8,000 / 16,000 rows took 15 / 35 / 100 / 321 / 1,225 ms (each doubling x2.2, 2.9, 3.2, 3.8, converging on x4), against a native table of the same rows at 3 / 4 / 6 / 10 / 20 ms. A CPU profile put the growth in the DOM's insertBefore (1.7 ms at 4,000 rows, 697 ms at 16,000). Deleting one rule, .p-datatable-tbody > tr:has(+ .p-datatable-row-selected) > td (angulux-styles/datatable), took 16,000 rows from 1,172 ms to 144 ms, the same as with every stylesheet disabled (139 ms). The gate holds the mechanism, not a timing a slow runner could flake. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.3 · TreeTable · 5188ee327f1f.note: Does NOT reproduce, measured 2026-11-02. Same sizes as the table: 35 / 64 / 140 / 368 / 892 ms (x1.8, 2.2, 2.6, 2.4) for flat nodes, and the same shape with nine expanded children per node. The treetable stylesheet loaded at runtime carries no :has() rule that looks at the next row, which is the difference from the table entry of the same release. The passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts holds on to that.

22.1.3 · Overlay · d1ba5cd100ac.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02. After an option is picked, a Select panel stays in place through its leave phase with pointer-events auto: hovering focuses another option and a click selects it. At the DEFAULT timing, sampled every frame, the panel stays hit-testable for about 320 ms after the selecting click, which a quick second click reaches. The gate stretches the leave phase to 1.5 s through motionOptions so the window is hit on purpose; the length of the window does not decide whether it takes pointer events. Overlay listeners are removed only in onOverlayAfterLeave. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.2 · ConfirmDialog · fa30946dc213.note: Does NOT reproduce, measured 2026-11-02. acceptIcon and rejectIcon render as <i class="pi pi-check"> and <i class="pi pi-times"> on the accept and reject buttons, both when set as inputs on <agl-confirmdialog> and when carried by the confirmation object. Kept as a passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts.

22.1.2 · DatePicker · a01f058bf31d.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, then FIXED 2026-11-03 under Constitution P3.a. On a 12-hour clock next to a bound; without a bound the buttons step correctly through noon. Four scenarios, all on 15 March 2026: (1) 4 PM, maxDate 5 PM, two increments: shows "17 PM", value 05:00 the NEXT DAY. (2) 1:45 PM, minDate 1:30 PM, one decrement: shows "13 PM", value 01:30 the NEXT DAY. (3) stepHour=2 back from 1 PM: 11 PM instead of 11 AM, since PM flips only on passing exactly 12. (4) 11 AM, maxDate 11:30 AM, one increment: 11:30 PM, twelve hours past the maximum. The clamps in incrementHour/decrementHour write 24-hour values into a 12-hour field and leave pm set. Silent, and the value lands outside the bound the app declared. Fix: the step and the clamp run on a 24-hour clock and only the result becomes a 12-hour hour, so every scenario lands where the 24-hour picker lands (min 13:30, max 17:00, 11 AM, 11:30 AM); datepicker.spec.ts asserts both clocks write the same instant. Held with test.fail() until the fix, one test per scenario.

22.1.1 · Table · 9155687471bf.note: Does NOT reproduce, measured 2026-11-02, in three shapes: lazy with no state, lazy with stateKey, and lazy with stateKey and reorderableColumns, each receiving its columns together with the first page from onLazyLoad. All render two header cells and two cells per row, before and after a reload restores the saved state (including a saved columnOrder). Kept as a passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts.

22.1.1 · Table · 9b82eeae3e1b.note: Does NOT reproduce, measured 2026-11-02. With a paginator and 20 rows, a menu column filter takes totalRecords to 2 and its Clear button back to 20; a row filter does the same when its text is emptied (it filters on Enter, the filterOn default). The paginator report follows both. Kept as a passing test in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts.

22.1.1 · Menu · 621fd8489601.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02, in part. Arrow keys move through items drawn by a custom #item template as they do without one. Activation does not: with a template drawing a plain <span>, Enter and Space run nothing. onEnterKey() clicks a link or button inside the item and otherwise clicks the <li>, but the click handler sits on the content element inside the <li>, which a click on the <li> never reaches. A template that draws an <a> is not affected. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.1 · Dialog · fa3ac51daa10.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02. [appendTo] set to an element puts the dialog's mask under document.body, not inside the element: any value other than 'self' appends to body. The input's own documentation names "a local ng-template variable of another element" as a valid value. appendTo="body" behaves as declared. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.

22.1.1 · DatePicker · 1843658c4d5a.note: REPRODUCED 2026-11-02. With a required FormControl, pressing the mouse on a day blurs the input, which calls onModelTouched while the control is still empty: an error gated on touched && invalid appears, and goes away when the click lands and the value is written (event order: touched, value, status). From the keyboard it lasts longer: ArrowDown moves focus into the grid, marks the control touched, and the error stays up while the user chooses. Held with test.fail() in e2e/upstream-repro-22-1.spec.ts; not fixed.
